subject: ACME - RAG evaluation follow-up & recommended models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Samira Patel <s.patel@acmecorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: ACME - RAG evaluation follow-up & recommended models

Hey Jamie —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Improve search-grounded answers in your support portal with RAG; reduce hallucination and increase precise grounding for policy/product questions.
- Current infra: ElasticSearch-backed vector store, 512-token chunks, proprietary embedding pipeline.
- Key success metrics you mentioned: precision@3 for grounding, reduction in manual escalations, average latency < 400ms (95th).

Initial model/retriever recommendations (based on what you shared):
1) Embedding: switch to redwood/embed-v2 (higher alignment for product docs).
2) Retriever: hybrid dense + BM25 with chunk_size = 400 tokens, overlap = 128 tokens (better recall on long product pages).
3) Generator (model variants):
   - Option A (low-latency): redwood/lex-7b-quant (8-bit q4_0) — good throughput, acceptable for most FAQ style answers.
   - Option B (higher-fidelity): redwood/opt-1.3 (16-bit) — better for complex policy Qs and long-context reasoning.
4) Reranker: a cross-encoder reranker (recommended: roberta-cross-encoder-v1 or similar) applied at top-10 retrievals; tune threshold to favor precision@1/3.

RAG-specific evals we propose running next:
- Grounding metrics: precision@k (k=1,3), groundedness rate (fraction of model tokens attributable to any source span), hallucination rate by category.
- Retrieval experiments: compare embedding models (your current vs redwood/embed-v2), chunk sizes (256/400/600), and hybrid vs dense-only.
- Reranker ablation: no-rerank vs lightweight mono-encoder vs cross-encoder.

Deliverables we'll share this week:
- Benchmark CSV with per-example ground-truth and model outputs (attached).
- Prompt set used for eval (attached prompt_set_v1).
- Short runbook for reproducing the eval (Drive link below).

Ask: Can you confirm the set of 200 evaluation queries we discussed (Samira will centralize them)? If yes, we’ll kick off the batch eval and share results + visualization(s) within 5 business days.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm eval query set (Samira).
2) Approve access to a snapshot of the Elastic index (read-only) so we can build a representative vector store (legal OK required).
3) Quick sync next Tue to review initial results.

Attachments: acme_rag_benchmark_results.csv (benchmark stub), acme_prompt_set_v1.md (prompt set).

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. Samira and I reviewed the recommendations briefly. A couple of clarifying Qs before we confirm the eval set:

1) For the reranker: can you share expected latency/compute tradeoffs between the mono-encoder approach vs cross-encoder? Our infra team will need numbers to size the Dedicated pool.
2) For embeddings: what privacy implications are there if we use redwood/embed-v2 vs our current proc? Any PII handling notes we should give Legal?

We can confirm the 200 queries by EOD Monday. Before you request read-only access, Legal wants a short list of artifacts you’ll need and the retention window.

Also — Samira asked if you can include a quick pricing estimate for both Option A and Option B generator configs at the scale of ~50k monthly active queries. That will help us prioritize.

Thanks — Jamie
Principal PM, Search & Knowledge, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jamie O'Neill <jamie.oneill@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <s.patel@acmecorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: ACME - RAG evaluation follow-up & recommended models

Jamie — great questions, answering inline below.

1) Reranker latency/compute:
- Mono-encoder (approx): 5–10 ms per pair on a single vCPU+GPU-accelerated embedding lookup; cheaper and scales well but lower precision for fine-grained ranking.
- Cross-encoder (approx): 35–120 ms per pair depending on model size (we typically run cross-encoder only on top-10 retrieved docs). For your SLA, we recommend cross-encoder as a reranker applied to top-10 (keeps tail latency within your 400ms SLO while improving precision@1/3).

I'll attach a short PDF with representative cost/latency numbers for both approaches (redwood_reranker_recommendations.pdf). These are estimates; we can run a quick perf test on a small sample to tighten numbers.

2) Embedding privacy:
- redwood/embed-v2 can be used in Private mode (VPC/on-prem) or with customer-managed keys when using Dedicated/Private. If you need to avoid any outgoing calls to hosted embeddings we can run the embedding model in your Dedicated pool. For Legal: artifacts requested are a read-only index snapshot (no PII export), a list of affected indices, and temporary access window (we recommend 7 days) — happy to formalize in an email to Legal.

3) Pricing sketch (very rough for 50k MAU):
- Option A (lex-7b-quant): lower per-token compute, estimated $X/month (we'll send a more precise HubSpot quote).
- Option B (opt-1.3): higher per-token cost but fewer re-runs for complex queries; estimated $Y/month.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll schedule a 30-min perf/pricing sync for Wed to review numbers and legal artifacts.
- Once Samira confirms the eval set, Connor and I will kick off the benchmark run.

Attachments: redwood_reranker_recommendations.pdf (latency/cost sketch), acme_rag_benchmark_results.csv (updated with header rows), acme_prompt_set_v1.md

Best,
Marissa

Quick note from infra/ops: when we run the cross-encoder reranker on top-10, we recommend batching the cross-encoder calls in micro-batches of 4–8 pairs to reduce GPU overhead. Also, set a hard timeout of 150ms per pair at the cross-encoder layer and fall back to mono-encoder score for any timeout to protect tail latency.

I'll add these defaults to the runbook before we hand it over to Acme.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
